sources.entry: GoatCounter - Easy web statistics without tracking of personal data. (Source Code) EUPL-1.2 Go
GoatCounter | Easy web analytics with no tracking of personal data

summary.one_liner: GoatCounter is an open source, privacy-friendly web analytics platform that can be used as a hosted service or self-hosted as a single Go application.
summary.what_it_does: It collects website statistics such as pageviews, browser, location, screen size, referring sites and campaigns, and identifies unique visits without cookies using a non-identifiable hash. Data can be gathered with a single JavaScript script tag, a no-JavaScript image tracking pixel, the HTTP/REST API from backend middleware, or by importing web server log files (nginx, Apache, Caddy, CloudFront and others). It can be self-hosted with an embedded web server, using SQLite by default or PostgreSQL as the database. The README describes TLS with automatic ACME certificate generation, a Docker image, a server management page, a /status health URL, and database migration commands. Data can be exported at any time.
use_cases: analyzing server log files for pageviews
running analytics in Docker or Podman
stack: C compiler (optional, needed for SQLite builds with cgo)
notable: Works without cookies or unique identifiers and states it does not need a GDPR consent notice
Can import and analyze existing web server log files
Single statically compiled binary with no required dependency beyond a SQLite file or PostgreSQL connection
Built-in TLS and automatic ACME certificate generation
Interface stated to work with screen readers and other assistive technology
caveats: The README notes performance depends on how spread out pageviews are across pages; SQLite may be slow for sites with very many distinct pages, where PostgreSQL is recommended
Building from source requires Go 1.21+ and a C compiler unless CGO_ENABLED=0 is used, which limits you to PostgreSQL
The author notes the main branch is reasonably stable but makes no guarantees and release notes may be missing, so upgrades may surprise you
keywords: track my site traffic without cookies
